newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caldera backs CVG sale scheme.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caldera backs CVG sale scheme.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera has given his full backing to the slated sale of iron and aluminum firms in state-holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG), government ministers said.
In a meeting Wednesday, Caldera "gave us his full support for the process," said Alberto Poletto, president of Venezuela's National Investment Fund, the body in charge of privatization.
Sales contracts for the CVG's four aluminum companies and iron firm Sidor are yet to be submitted to congress, where they are expected to meet stiff opposition.

But Poletto told reporters at Miraflores Presidential Palace "there's absolutely no doubt we'll go ahead with the sales", adding "they'll not be sold off cheap, if they were, I too would be against it." Poletto did not provide a sale price estimate.

Poletto was accompanied by Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar, who confirmed earlier reports that the aluminum firms would be placed in a holding company before the privatisation. Seamless steel-tubing company Tuborca would meanwhile be sold off separately as it still required some $300 million of investments to begin operations.
